description:
Calculate the design heat loss of a single room in watts, following BS EN 12831 as
MIS 3005-D applies it. This is the figure a heat pump is sized from and the figure the radiator in
that room must be able to deliver.

BS EN 12831 is a room-by-room method. Run this once for each heated room and add the results; sizing
a heat pump from floor area alone is what produces the oversized installations that cycle all winter.

Internal design temperatures come from Table 1 of MIS 3005-D and follow from the room type: 22 for a
bathroom, 21 for living and dining rooms, 18 for bedrooms, halls, kitchens and toilets. These are
minimums, so a higher figure is accepted and a lower one is refused.

External design temperatures come from Table 2, for eight locations, in two columns: 'a' is the 99%
figure and 'b' the colder 99.6% one, which needs no uplift for intermittent heating.

Each element needs an area, a U-value, and a kind. The kind matters because it fixes which temperature
difference applies. Walls, windows, doors, roofs and suspended floors lose heat to the outside design
temperature. A SOLID FLOOR ON THE GROUND loses heat to the local annual average air temperature
instead, which is far warmer, and getting this wrong is the commonest error in a heat loss calculation.
Window and door areas belong to the window and the door, not to the wall behind them.

Method from MIS 3005-D. These calculators follow the published MCS methods, for understanding a system and checking a quotation. Anything that gets installed still needs a design and a site survey from a certified installer.

airChangesPerHour.description: How many times an hour the air in the room is replaced. A draughty old room may be 1.5 or more; a well sealed new one 0.5. Defaults to 1.

ceilingHeightM.description: Floor to ceiling height in metres. Defaults to 2.4.

designBasis.description: 'a' for the 99% outside design temperature or 'b' for the colder 99.6% figure. Column B needs no uplift for intermittent heating. Defaults to 'a'.

elements.description: Every surface through which the room loses heat. At least one is required.

areaM2.description: Area of the element in square metres. Window and door areas are taken out of the wall area, not counted twice. Required.

label.description: A name for this element, so the result can be read back against the survey.

uValue.description: U-value in W/m2K: the watts lost through each square metre for every degree of temperature difference. Required.

unheatedTemp.description: Temperature of the unheated space on the other side, in Celsius. Only used for the 'unheated_space' kind. Defaults to halfway between inside and outside.

floorAreaM2.description: Floor area of the room in square metres. Required, and used with the ceiling height to work out the ventilation loss.

internalTemp.description: Internal design temperature in Celsius, if it should differ from the tabulated value for the room type. MIS 3005-D sets the tabulated values as a floor, not a target, so a higher figure is allowed and a lower one is not.

location.description: Which of the eight tabulated locations the property is nearest: 'belfast', 'birmingham', 'cardiff', 'edinburgh', 'glasgow', 'london', 'manchester' or 'plymouth'. Required.

roomType.description: Which of the tabulated room types this is: 'living_room', 'dining_room', 'bedsitting_room', 'bathroom', 'bedroom', 'kitchen', 'hall' or 'toilet'. Sets the internal design temperature. Defaults to 'living_room'.

name: room_heat_loss

largestLoss.description: Which single element loses most, which is where insulating first pays best.

designTempA.description: Hourly dry-bulb temperature exceeded for 99% of the hours in a year.

designTempB.description: The colder 99.6% figure. Using it removes the need for any uplift for intermittent heating.

temperatureDifference.description: Internal minus external design temperature, in kelvin. The figure most of the fabric loss is worked out against.

totalHeatLossW.description: The room's design heat loss in watts. This is what the emitter in the room has to deliver on the coldest day.

wattsPerSquareMetre.description: Heat loss divided by floor area. A useful sanity check: a well insulated room lands near 40, a poor one well over 100.

title: Room heat loss
